content:
Do you want to replace a Microsoft e-mail client, e.g., Outlook on Windows, or do you want to replace a Microsoft account or both?

You cannot switch from outlook.office.com to Thunderbird. You can switch from accessing your outlook.office.com account in one e-mail client, e.g., Outlook (or webmail), to a different e-mail client, e.g., Thunderbird. And you can switch from using outlook.office.com to using a different account from a different e-mail service provider, e.g., Gmail.

If you want to replace a Microsoft e-mail client with Thunderbird, that is easy, but transferring messages that were saved locally in your old e-mail client will require some effort and maybe expense.

If you want to replace your Microsoft 365 account, you will have to establish a new account with some e-mail service provider, then set up the new account in Thunderbird. And you would need a plan for transferring the messages from the old account to the new account.

Where the domain is hosted is independent or other considerations. My domain and my e-mail are hosted by different services.

Regardless of what you do with e-mail clients, your business e-mail account should always work in webmail.

"Email" has come to mean three different things. I do not know if you are asking about accounts or messages. You can move one account at a time on your own schedule. I think that's what you wanted to know.

If you are running Windows 7 then you are probably using a very old version of Thunderbird.

The last version of Thunderbird that can run on Windows 7 is version 115.18.0esr Q: What version are you using ? Q: Are you talking about an Imap or Pop mail account?

When you delete or move emails from eg: Inbox - they get 'marked as deleted' and hidden from view. They may reappear in the Trash or whatever folder they were moved to. However, the Inbox still has the original in the mbox file and that file needs to be tidied up/basic housekeeping maintenance to fully remove those emails.

Q: do you compact the folder after doing a load of deleting etc ? The three folders that proboably need to be compacted on a more regular basis especially after doing a load of deleting are Inbox, Drafts, Junk/Spam

  • Right click on folder and select Compact.

Whilst compacting is occuring do not select to use that folder and do not exit thunderbird.

re :the messages go from displaying in bold to displaying as read messages; but them are still displayed.

Displayed where ? Are they still displaying in the Inbox - do they have a strikethrough or displaying in the Trash ? When you delete it should go to the server Trash folder.

  • In Account Settings > Server Settings' for the account
  • 'When I delete a message' - What have you got selected ?

IMAP account - select 'Move it to this folder' and select the server Trash folder on account.

Q: Is the imap Trash folder set up to get updated?

  • Right click on imap Trash folder and select 'Properties'
  • Is this checkbox selected ? 'When getting new messages for this account, always check this folder'

If no, then select it.


'Q:What Anti-Virus product do you use ? Is it allowed to scan every file that gets opened or upload to and from server? That can be a pain and cause all kinds of interference issues. content: Thunderbird does not read MSG files directly because MSG is an Outlook email format. The easy fix is to convert MSG into EML first, then open the converted emails in Thunderbird. For this, you can use a dedicated tool like Softaken MSG to EML Converter. It converts MSG files into EML or EMLX format and keeps the email content, structure, formatting, and properties safe. It also supports bulk MSG conversion, so multiple Outlook MSG files can be handled together. After conversion, you can easily import an EML file into Thunderbird.
